🎓 Scholar or Ignoramus — 'by His goodness' vs 'from His goodness', and other tell-tale phrasings of the zimmun
🔢 Ten or Ten Thousand — Rabbi Yosei HaGelili vs Rabbi Akiva on the size of the crowd; Rava's ruling
🔁 No Retroactive Zimmun — three who may not divide, three from three groups, and Rava's proof from a broken bed

overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Words of the Zimmun and the Dignity of Food
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 50a–50b
overview.hebrewSource: וּמִבִּרְכוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם נִיכָּר אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא אִם לָאו
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf concludes that 'Let us bless' is the better zimmun formula because the leader includes himself, then lists phrasings that reveal whether the speaker is a Torah scholar or an ignoramus. It resolves the contradiction in the mishna about crowd size — Rabbi Yosei HaGelili scales the formula, Rabbi Akiva does not, and Rava rules like Rabbi Akiva. A new mishna teaches that three who ate together may not divide, six may divide until ten, and ten may not until twenty; Rava adds that once people were included in a zimmun their obligation 'flies away', proving it from a bed that was split and rejoined. The daf closes with wine that has not been diluted, four rules about honoring bread, and what to do with food already in one's mouth when a blessing was forgotten.

slides.title: 🗣️ Why 'Let Us Bless' Beats 'Bless'
slides.subtitle: Finishing Shmuel's rule: never exclude yourself from the collective

nodes.content: ❓ The mishna says that with three and himself one says 'Bless'. Doesn't that exclude the leader from the group?
💬 Answer: the mishna means he may say 'Bless' — but 'Let us bless' (נְבָרֵךְ) is preferable.
📜 Proof — Rav Adda bar Ahava, from the school of Rav: six may divide into two zimmun groups, up to ten.

columns.label: If nevarekh is preferable
columns.content: Then dividing loses nothing — each group of three can still say 'Let us bless'.

columns.label: If barekhu were preferable
columns.content: Why permit dividing? Neither group of three could say 'Bless' (which needs three besides the leader).

nodes.content: ✅ Conclude: 'Let us bless' is preferable. The Tosefta agrees — whoever says either is not reprimanded, though the punctilious do reprimand him.

slides.title: 🎓 A Man's Blessings Reveal Whether He Is a Scholar
slides.subtitle: Phrasings of the zimmun that mark a talmid ḥakham or a bur
rows: 'From' implies only part of God's goodness reached him — a denial of His kindness. David's 'from Your blessing' (II Sam. 7:29) is a request, which is different; 'open your mouth wide' (Ps. 81:11) applies to Torah
'They' excludes the speaker from the collective. The Sages of Neharbela taught the reverse, but the halakha does not follow them
'Let us bless the One Whose food we have eaten' (Rabbi Yoḥanan)
'Let us bless to Him from Whose food we have eaten'
'To him' sounds like a blessing for the host. At the seder 'to Him Who performed miracles' is fine — only God performs miracles (Rav Ashi to Rav Aḥa son of Rava)
'Blessed is the One from Whose food we have eaten' (Rabbi Yoḥanan)
It again sounds as if he blesses the host
Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua: these rules apply only with three
With ten, God's name is invoked — 'Blessed is the Lord our God… for the food we have eaten' — so it is self-evident to Whom the blessing is directed

slides.title: 🔢 Does the Formula Grow with the Crowd?
slides.subtitle: The mishna says ten equals ten myriads — and then gives different words for a hundred, a thousand, and ten thousand

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: The mishna contradicts itself: 'both ten and ten myriads' — so they are the same; then 'with a hundred he says… with a thousand… with ten thousand…' — so it depends on the number!

lines.speaker: Rav Yosef
lines.text: Not difficult. This is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, that is Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: bless according to the size of the crowd — 'In assemblies bless God' (Ps. 68:27). Rabbi Akiva: as in the synagogue, many or few say 'Bless the Lord'.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: What does Rabbi Akiva do with 'In assemblies bless God'?

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: He needs it for Rabbi Meir's teaching: even fetuses in their mothers' wombs sang at the sea. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili derives that from 'from the source of Israel', an allusion to the womb.

lines.speaker: Ravina
lines.text: At the Exilarch's banquet Rav Ḥama bar Buzi rose to gather a hundred diners. Ravina told him: no need — Rava ruled like Rabbi Akiva; the formula is the same from ten upward.

callout.label: More from the Exilarch's house and the synagogue:
callout.text: Rava: at the Exilarch's we recited Grace in groups of three — groups of ten would anger the Exilarch, and the noise kept anyone from hearing his blessing. Rafram bar Pappa said 'Bless the Lord' without 'the blessed One', and the whole synagogue shouted the full formula; Rava told him, 'black pot, why involve yourself in the dispute? The world's custom follows Rabbi Yishmael.'

slides.title: 🔁 Three May Not Divide — and No Retroactive Zimmun
slides.subtitle: The new mishna and Rava's proof from a broken bed

steps.content: 1️⃣ Mishna: three who ate together may not divide; likewise four and five. Six may divide, up to ten; ten may not divide until twenty. Two groups in one house join if some of them can see each other

2️⃣ What is new? We already learned that three must form a zimmun! Rabbi Abba in Shmuel's name: even three who merely sat down to eat and have not yet eaten may not divide — or, in another version, even if each eats from his own loaf
3️⃣ Alternatively, Rav Huna's rule: three who came from three different groups may not divide. Rav Ḥisda: only if each came from a group of three, so the obligation never lapsed
4️⃣ Rava: and only if their original groups did not already include them in a zimmun. If they did — פְּרַח זִימּוּן מִינַּיְיהוּ, the zimmun obligation has flown away from them

5️⃣ Rava's proof: an impure bed half stolen, lost, or divided by brothers or partners is pure; if restored it becomes susceptible to impurity from now on, not retroactively. Once divided, the impurity left — so too, once included in a zimmun, the obligation left
6️⃣ Rabba Tosefa'a: if one of three went ahead and recited Grace alone, the other two fulfill their zimmun with him, but he gains nothing from theirs — there is no retroactive zimmun
7️⃣ Baraita on two groups: if a common waiter serves both, the waiter joins them into one group

slides.title: 🍷 Wine, Bread, and Food in the Mouth
slides.subtitle: The daf's closing halakhot on the dignity of what we eat

boxes.title: Undiluted wine
items: Rabbi Eliezer: before water is added, bless 'fruit of the tree' and one may wash hands with it; after — 'fruit of the vine', and no washing
The Rabbis: either way it is wine — 'fruit of the vine', and no washing
Shmuel's 'one may do all his needs with bread' follows Rabbi Eliezer
Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina: the Rabbis concede for a cup of blessing — Rav Oshaya: we want the mitzva done in the best manner
Rabbi Zeira: undiluted wine is fit for koraiytei, a wine-and-oil remedy

boxes.title: Respect for bread
items: Four rules: no raw meat on bread, no passing a full cup over bread, no throwing bread, no propping a dish with bread
Mar Zutra tossed a pomegranate to Rav Ashi; the baraitot conflict about throwing other foods
Resolution: food that becomes disgusting when thrown may not be thrown; food that does not, may
Wine may be piped before a bride and groom; roasted grain and nuts thrown in summer but not the rainy season; cakes never

boxes.title: Food in the mouth without a blessing
items: Rav Yehuda: move it to one side of the mouth and recite the blessing
Three baraitot: swallow — liquids, no alternative
Spit out — food that does not become disgusting and can still be eaten
Move aside — food that would become disgusting

summary.principle: The wording of the zimmun must include the speaker and point clearly to God; a zimmun obligation, once discharged, cannot be revived; and food — wine, bread, or anything else — must be treated with respect.

flowSteps.content: 🗣️ 'Let us bless' is preferable to 'Bless' — proved because six may divide into two groups
🎓 'By His goodness we live', 'the One Whose food we have eaten' — a scholar; 'from His goodness', 'they live', 'to him', 'for the food' — an ignoramus
🔢 Rabbi Yosei HaGelili scales the formula to the crowd; Rabbi Akiva does not — Rava: halakha like Rabbi Akiva

columns.content: 🔁 Three may not divide; once included in a zimmun the obligation flies away (Rava's broken bed)
🍷 Cup of blessing needs water even per the Rabbis; bread is not thrown or used as a prop

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: There is no retroactive zimmun — one who blessed alone helps the others but cannot be helped by them

quiz.q: How does the Gemara prove that 'Let us bless' is preferable to 'Bless'?
o: Because the Tosefta explicitly reprimands one who says 'Bless'
Because a group of six may divide into two zimmun groups, which would be pointless if 'Bless' were preferable
Because Shmuel forbade saying 'Bless' altogether
Because the mishna never mentions 'Bless'
quiz.e: Rav Adda bar Ahava taught that six to ten may divide. If 'Bless' were the better formula, dividing would be pointless since neither group of three could say it; therefore 'Let us bless' must be preferable.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, why is one who says 'and from His goodness we live' considered an ignoramus?
o: Because it copies King David's language, which only a king may use
Because it implies that only some of God's goodness was bestowed on him, tantamount to denying His kindness
Because it excludes the speaker from the collective
Because it sounds like he is blessing the host
quiz.e: 'From His goodness' suggests a limited portion of God's goodness. Abaye's objection from David's 'from Your blessing' is answered: a request is different, and 'open your mouth wide' refers to Torah.

quiz.q: What did Ravina tell Rav Ḥama bar Buzi when he tried to gather a hundred diners at the Exilarch's banquet?
o: That the Exilarch would be angry
That a hundred requires the formula 'the God of Israel'
That there is no need, since Rava ruled like Rabbi Akiva and the formula is the same from ten upward
That they should instead bless in groups of three
quiz.e: Rava ruled that the halakha follows Rabbi Akiva: the zimmun formula does not change with the size of the crowd once there are ten, so there was no reason to assemble a hundred.

quiz.q: What does Rava prove from the mishna about a bed that was half stolen and later restored?
o: That utensils never regain impurity once purified
That two groups in one house may combine for a zimmun
That once people were included in a zimmun, their obligation has left them and does not return, just as the bed's impurity does not return retroactively
That three who sat down to eat may not divide
quiz.e: The restored bed becomes susceptible to impurity only from then on, not retroactively — the impurity 'flew away' when it was divided. Likewise, once the original groups included the three in a zimmun, their zimmun obligation flew away.

quiz.q: Why do the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Eliezer that a cup of blessing requires added water?
o: Because undiluted wine is not 'fruit of the vine'
Because a mitzva should be performed in the best possible manner
Because one may wash hands only with undiluted wine
Because undiluted wine is fit only for koraiytei
quiz.e: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina says the Rabbis concede for a cup of blessing, and Rav Oshaya gives the reason: we require the mitzva to be done in the choicest way.
